evals.prompt: I'm sending 500 cold emails a day from my main domain and getting no replies.
evals.expected_output: Should diagnose deliverability, not copy: 500/day from a main domain far exceeds the 50-100 per mailbox safe limit and will trigger rate limiting and spam classification. Should warn about burning the primary domain. Should prescribe secondary domains, SPF/DKIM/DMARC, ~3 weeks warmup. Should note deliverability sets the ceiling and rewriting the email will not fix it.
assertions: Cites the 50-100 per mailbox per day limit
Warns about damaging the primary sending domain
States that copy changes will not fix an infrastructure problem

evals.prompt: I emailed 40 prospects once and nobody replied. Cold email doesn't work.
evals.expected_output: Should identify the actual problem: stopping after one touch. 58% of replies come from step one, meaning 42% come from follow-ups, and 80% of sales require 5+ touches while most founders stop after 2. Should also note 40 is too small a sample at a 3.43% average reply rate. Should redirect to warm intros first, which convert at 30-50% versus 2-5% cold.
assertions: Identifies insufficient follow-up as the problem
Cites that 42% of replies come from follow-ups
Notes 40 sends is too small a sample given a ~3.43% average
Contrasts warm intro conversion (30-50%) with cold (2-5%)
Recommends exhausting the existing network first
Does not accept the conclusion that cold email does not work
